summary: Implemented. A recipe carrying published_answer with publication.status 'published' is rendered as the reading text; the old assembly from recipe.decision/product survives untouched as the fallback for packs without an article, and a recipe without one renders exactly as before. Order is the producer's: standfirst, then the map, then a prominent "What to do now" card with recommendation.summary and numbered recommendation.steps, then a "Where" field checklist, then "What was measured", "What was estimated" (estimate.name shown as the method name with estimate.plain_language beneath it), "How the estimate was tested" (test.outcome as words in a bordered pill — never colour alone, and an unrecognised outcome is humanised rather than shown as a machine token), and "Why we are not giving stronger advice" carrying why_this_advice under that plain heading. publication.credit and published_at head the article; contributors are shown only when supplied and never invented. Every named_locations entry renders as a compact checklist row with its label and instruction; clicking one finds the matching feature by scanning drawn features for that id in any property (the id's property name is the pack's business), pans to it and flashes it — no query, no recompute, no value changed — and a location the map does not carry is marked unfound while staying readable. named_locations.role drives only generic wording and treatment (act / check first / measure first / do not act). All article prose is inserted as text; no innerHTML is used anywhere in the article path. "How this map was tested" and full provenance remain after the article as the technical audit. The Themes centre runs the article's declared default_arguments so note and map describe the same run, and publishedAnswer() withholds the article when the arguments differ, so a rerun never inherits the default article. Validation stays authoritative: a failed or pending result still suppresses selected styling regardless of article prose, and TR-VIS-0009's validation-priority treatment carries partial articles. Open in chat now carries the standfirst, measured evidence, named estimator, plain-language test, recommendation with steps, named location ids with roles, why_this_advice, credit, data sets with DOIs and the result id — never the mechanically assembled write-up when an article exists.
consumer_note: Acceptance verified live at 1440x1000. Recorder theme: opens naming OLCAP3B, OLV208U, PANMP3B, SEL207R, STIN02U and UPMAP1B, visibly names "Twelve-nearest-neighbour regression", labels the test "The test did not pass", and marks the six as measure-first evidence requests with zero selections. Invasive theme: names all eight plots including the Candura comparison plot, outcome "Not yet testable", eight evidence marks. Mother-tree theme: "The test passed", ten trees under the selected-budget treatment with role "check first". Rhythm and corridor articles read from their partial cards. Clicking a named location focuses the producer feature and flashes it. Two observations for the producer: (1) test.outcome uses 'not-yet-testable' which is not in the validation status vocabulary ('pending'), so the consumer maps it to "Not yet testable" and humanises any future unseen value — a shared vocabulary would be cleaner; (2) the consumer had to key the location lookup on 'any string property equals location_id' because the catalogue does not say which feature property carries the id; a declared id field per layer would make the match exact rather than heuristic.
producer_action_required: Optional: declare which feature property carries a named location's id (e.g. style_hint.feature_id_field), so the checklist match is exact rather than a property scan.
Optional: align test.outcome with the validation status vocabulary, or declare the allowed outcome values, so 'not-yet-testable' does not need consumer-side mapping.
